t2ogxay.name: US-Iran war and Hormuz
t2ogxay.latestHeadline: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles off north coast of Qatar, UKMTO says
t2ogxay.summary: On 2 October, The Guardian reported that the US was sending a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East amid a stalemate in the Iran war. By 5 October, Al Jazeera reported that Middle East oil exports had passed pre-war levels, while an IRGC commander called oil flows through a US-supervised route in Hormuz 'negligible', and The Guardian reported that Iran's oil minister had resigned amid a worsening economic crisis. On 6 October, Saudi Arabia said its East-West pipeline was pumping 5.8 million barrels per day after a major attack the previous month, and on 7 October Oman evacuated injured crew from an attacked tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, with India's Foreign Ministry saying 11 of the 12 injured were Indian nationals. t1kqejni.name: Protests over India election chief
t1kqejni.latestHeadline: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
t1kqejni.summary: On 2 October, thousands of people attended a protest in Mumbai called by the Cockroach Janta Party, asking the election chief to resign. By 4 October, police had detained dozens of protesters demanding his resignation over changes to voter rolls, and police were accused of sexually harassing journalists at the protest. On 6 October, opposition MPs were detained in a protest against the election chief, with opposition leaders alleging that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated voter rolls to favour PM Narendra Modi's party.

t1uohici.name: Diesel reserves and US export ban
t1uohici.latestHeadline: Shell expects refineries to almost double the profit from every barrel of fuel made
t1uohici.summary: In early October, President Donald Trump threatened to ban diesel exports to ease prices in the US ahead of the November elections, and the US pressed Europe to release its diesel reserves. A couple of days later, G7 nations agreed to release large amounts of diesel fuel, though European countries were not entirely happy about the agreement. In the days after that, Shell said it expected its refineries to make record profits on each barrel of fuel produced, as shortages linked to the shutdown of war-damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia pushed pump prices around the world to all-time highs.

t1j5n1me.name: Yemen war and Houthi strikes
t1j5n1me.latestHeadline: Saudi Arabia says three wounded in attacks on airports near Yemen border
t1j5n1me.summary: In early October, Yemen's president announced an all-out war to reclaim land from the Houthis, a move that came amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition. A couple of days later, Saudi Arabia said three people were wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border. The Saudi aviation authority reported severe injuries and damage following Houthi strikes on the two airports.

t14axxk2.name: Black Sea shipping attacks
t14axxk2.latestHeadline: Black Sea tanker attack off Russia's Olympic city sparks 'fire of oil'
t14axxk2.summary: In early October, Ukraine's leader Zelensky condemned a Russian strike on a Turkish-owned boat carrying corn in the Black Sea, in which the captain was killed and 11 crew members were rescued. The next day, Bulgaria launched a search for missing crew after drones hit two ships in the Black Sea and the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank at the scene of the attack. On October 7, Russian authorities said an attack by "unmanned boats" on a Liberian-flagged tanker off the coast of Sochi sparked a giant "fire of oil".

t1ibmsov.name: Russia fuel crisis and refinery strikes
t1ibmsov.latestHeadline: Has Russia’s fuel crisis given Iranian oil an opening in Central Asia?
t1ibmsov.summary: In early October, Ukraine's top sanctions official said Russia had imported fuel from South Korean ports, which eased the impact of a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. The next day, Al Jazeera reported that Iran's oil exports have struggled amid a US blockade, and that the Russian energy crisis resulting from the Ukrainian attacks could help Iran.
